newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to up, pork bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to up, pork bellies mixed.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent a lb higher while calls ranged from 0.250 cent a lb higher to 0.200 lower for pork belly futures, livestock analysts said.

Snow and falling temperatures over parts of the Midwest were expected to provide early strength in hog futures. Higher pork cutout values linked to higher loin and ham prices should also lend support, analysts said.
However, some analysts considered futures overbought after Friday's sharp advance in nearbys. Poor weather is already in the market, they said.

Calls on pork belly futures ranged mixed as fundamentals pointed in both directions. The light pace of slaughter, running five percent under a year ago, and light storage indications looked supportive while an easier tone to cash bellies late in the week may weigh on demand, they said.
Hog slaughter last week ran about five percent under the year-ago level but failed to keep product values from slipping by Friday, they said.
Technically, the market still is pointing higher, which may lend support, some sources noted.
